世界音樂樂團（World Music Ensemble）— 把不同傳統的樂器放上: World Music Ensemble — a cross-cultural line-up that puts instruments from different traditions on one stage and works by compromise in arrangement and tuning. Ensembles and instrumentation by Next Door Sound Weavers.
世界音樂樂團（world music ensemble）不是某一種音樂傳統，而是: The world music ensemble is not a musical tradition but a performance line-up that took shape in European and North American cities in the late twentieth century: instruments and players from different traditions put into one group, playing for festivals, theatres, cultural centres and the record market. Its reason for existing is not a court or a ritual but the demand of that market — that different musics can be placed side by side on one stage.

傳統合奏的改編大多藏在口傳與即興裡，由樂手當場完成；但這個樂團的樂器組合每次不同: In traditional ensembles most arrangement is hidden in oral transmission and improvisation, done on the spot by the players; but this band's combination of instruments is different every time, so someone has to decide in advance which part goes to whom, in which key, which ornaments are kept and which dropped. The arranger is not a composer but more like a translator and a negotiator: they have to understand the grammar of both sides and know which side can give way. Give the same melody to a kora or to a violin and the breathing and the ornaments are completely different; the arranger has to choose an approach that stands up on both sides.
優先找現場錄音。這類樂團的音量平衡大多由音控完成，錄音室版本會把這個過程藏起來，: Look for live recordings first. This kind of band's volume balance is mostly done by the engineer, and studio versions hide that process, so you cannot hear the differences in volume the instruments have by nature.

先說音高參考。不同傳統的樂器有不同的基準頻率，有些樂器又是固定音高——木琴、青銅: Pitch reference first. Instruments from different traditions have different reference frequencies, and some instruments are fixed in pitch — a xylophone, a bronze metallophone, some flutes, once made, hold their pitch. Strings and winds can be adjusted; fixed-pitch instruments cannot. When the two kinds share a stage, the reference is usually set by the side that cannot adjust, and the others come to it. This is not an aesthetic choice but a physical limit. So the same piece may sound slightly high in one band and slightly low in another, and both think they are playing in the same key.
出現在音樂節、文化中心、劇院、大學巡演，也出現在舞廳與錄音室。曲目大致分三類：傳: They appear at festivals, cultural centres, theatres and university tours, and also in dance halls and studios. The repertoire falls roughly into three kinds: arrangements of traditional material, cross-cultural pieces the band writes itself, and pieces written for a particular collaboration. The third shows the nature of this line-up best: the music is written for these few people and these few instruments, and a different group of people means writing it again. Many bands therefore keep two sets at once — a fixed repertoire they can take anywhere, and a temporary repertoire that appears only in a particular collaboration.
和電子原聲混合編制相比，差別在平衡由誰完成。電子原聲編制把擴音、即時處理與固定音: Compared with an electroacoustic line-up, the difference is who completes the balance. An electroacoustic line-up treats amplification, live processing and fixed tracks as material on one level, and the sound engineer is a member of the group, deciding the placing and layering of sound; in a world music ensemble amplification is mainly there to bridge the volume differences the instruments have by nature, letting a loud drum and a quiet string instrument coexist, and the engineer works on balance, not on the structure of the work.

Understand it as a genre and you find nothing in common; understand it as a way of producing music and you see the three lines of arrangement, tuning and market.

排練時真正的爭論通常不是音符，而是調音。一個音高幾赫茲的差異，會決定整首曲子聽起: The real arguments in rehearsal are usually not about notes but about tuning. A difference of a few hertz in pitch decides whether a piece sounds in tune or wrong. So the players check the same note over and over: am I high, or are you low? In an orchestra this conversation is handled by the leader and the oboe; here it is daily work that everyone takes part in.

最容易被當成管弦樂團的變體。兩者都有指揮或領奏、都在音樂廳與音樂節演出，但管弦樂: The one most easily taken for a variant of the orchestra. Both have a conductor or a leader and both play in concert halls and at festivals, but the orchestra relies on fixed proportions of parts and on long familiarity between players, and its instruments belong to one tuning system; the world music ensemble's line-up shifts with the repertoire, players are called in piece by piece beyond the core, pitch and tuning have to be negotiated for each piece, and the biggest part of the work is arranging, not rehearsing.

注意持續音。很多改編用一條持續的低音或簧風琴長音，把不同音律的樂器黏在一起；持續: Notice the sustained tones. Many arrangements use a sustained bass or a long harmonium note to glue instruments of different tuning systems together; the moment the sustained tone disappears is often the moment the whole group is least stable.
為了共存，經常整首移調，或把固定音高的樂器換成另一組。聽到「原聲」不等於聽到「原: To coexist, they often transpose the whole piece, or swap the fixed-pitch instruments for another set. Hearing the original sound does not mean hearing the original key, and that difference is exactly what needs most negotiation in this line-up.

第二是音律。平均律、純律、各種模態音階在同一個舞台上相遇時，有琴格的樂器無法做出: Second, the tuning system. When equal temperament, just intonation and various modal scales meet on one stage, a fretted instrument cannot make the note between two frets, while an unfretted string instrument or a voice can. So the arranger has to decide: simplify the ornaments, replace them with neighbouring notes, or transpose the whole passage into a key the fixed-pitch instruments can play. Listeners often think they are hearing the original piece, when the melody may already have changed key and half the ornaments been deleted. This compromise is rarely printed in the programme, yet it is what takes the most rehearsal time.
節奏也要翻譯。以循環為單位的音樂要放進有拍號的譜面；沒有固定拍子的音樂則需要提示: Rhythm has to be translated too. Music counted in cycles has to go onto a page with time signatures; music without a fixed beat needs cues. A common solution is to keep the original cycle but mark it with the drums or the bass so that everyone has a shared reference. Another is to compress the cycle into a repeating figure of a few bars, so that players unfamiliar with this music can count it. The price is that the original long structure is cut short and sounds more like a theme than like the whole ceremony.
編制浮動的原因很直接：每個曲目來自不同傳統，需要的樂器不同。樂團的實際組合往往由: The line-up shifts for a simple reason: each piece comes from a different tradition and needs different instruments. The band's actual combination is usually decided by what is being played this season, not by its constitution. Hence the two-tier structure common in such groups: a fixed core, and players around it who join for particular pieces.
編曲者在這個編制裡是一個獨立角色，原因就在這裡。: The arranger is an independent role in this line-up, and this is why.
聽打擊樂什麼時候進來。它通常是全團真正鎖在一起的那一刻；在此之前，各聲部常常是各: Listen to when the percussion comes in. It is usually the moment the whole group really locks together; before that the parts are often floating separately.
聽旋律被移調的痕跡。同一段旋律在兩個傳統裡可能相差好幾個音，注意編曲者怎麼處理音: Listen for the traces of transposition. The same melody may differ by several notes in two traditions; notice how the arranger handles leaps of a large interval.
與甘美朗相比，差別在調音的單位。甘美朗是一整套樂器一起製作、一起調音，換一個樂團: Compared with gamelan, the difference is the unit of tuning. Gamelan is a whole set of instruments made together and tuned together, and a different gamelan means a different set of pitches; a world music ensemble puts separately tuned instruments together and compromises on a shared reference, usually one decided by the fixed-pitch instruments that cannot be adjusted.

這種雙軌曲目也影響排練方式。固定曲目靠反覆演出磨合，樂手對彼此的習慣熟到可以即興: This two-track repertoire affects rehearsal too. The fixed repertoire is worn in by repeated performance, until the players know each other's habits well enough to improvise; temporary repertoire has to settle the most important few things in limited rehearsal — who leads, where it turns, what key. Experienced bands write the structure of temporary pieces very plainly, marking only sections and cues and leaving the rest to the moment. This is close to how jazz bands work, with one extra layer: the cues have to work for players with different notational habits at the same time, so a spoken instruction is often more reliable than a page.
這類樂團沒有標準編制，常見的是一個小型核心，加上依曲目邀請的合作樂手。分工不按交: These bands have no standard line-up; the usual thing is a small core plus players invited for particular repertoire. The division is not by an orchestra's logic of parts but by who supplies time, who supplies bass, who supplies melody, who supplies timbre. The same person may change role from piece to piece.
還有一層是空間。這類樂團常在沒有良好聲學的場地演出，音量大的鼓與音量小的弦樂器原: One more layer is the space. Such bands often play venues without good acoustics, where a loud drum and a quiet string instrument could never balance, so part of the balancing is handed to amplification. This changes how the players hear themselves: what they hear is not the instruments' natural sound but the sound after microphones and speakers. So how loud is correct stops being a matter between players and becomes a matter between players and the engineer. This is also why rehearsal in this kind of line-up often spends half its time on sound rather than on notes.
